clue.text: Page left out of, fool's travel document

indicators.note: the page-and-left pair sits on the outside of the fool, so they wrap around it

parts.note: port is the nautical word for left
an ass is a fool; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone foolish has torn a page from their travel papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' reads like removal, but here it means the page and left sit outside the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official booklet carried when crossing borders.

clue.text: Hot water finally added in one's cups

parts.note: to be in hot water or in a pickle is to be in trouble

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word added

explanation.surface: A drinker topping up with hot water, already merry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for being drunk.

clue.text: Pair one's insured are taken unawares

annotationWithheld.why: Pair one's insured are taken unawares (9): PR + IS inside SURED needs 'insured' read as IN + SURED, so the one word is both the insertion signal and the letters SURED
annotationWithheld.clue: Pair one's insured are taken unawares

clue.text: Set old boy up for psychological treatment

parts.note: to set something is to place it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the old boy abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An old boy is set up for therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill works only through the patient's belief, so its effect is in the mind.

clue.text: Habitual routine involves group making badge

indicators.note: involves means the routine wraps around the group

parts.note: rote is mechanical, habitual repetition
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A group's regular routine is making badges.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded at shows or worn by party supporters.

clue.text: Border priest introducing dean

indicators.note: the priest comes first, introducing the dean who follows

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
W. R. Inge, the 'gloomy dean', was a famous Dean of St Paul's

explanation.surface: A priest introducing a dean at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dean' is a specific dean: Inge, Dean of St Paul's Cathedral in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe is the edge or margin of something.

clue.text: Connoisseur retains fashionable money man

indicators.note: retains means the connoisseur holds the fashionable word inside

parts.note: a fancier is an enthusiast or connoisseur, as in pigeon fancier
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A connoisseur keeping up with fashion turns out to be a money man.
explanation.definitionFit: A financier deals in large-scale funding and investment.

clue.text: Capital opening for Croesus?

explanation.surface: A rich king's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital letter starting a name, and C is the first letter of Croesus.

clue.text: Liquid capacity is about a quarter in a large vessel

indicators.note: is about means the liquid measure surrounds the quarter

parts.note: a gallon is a measure of liquid capacity
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A big ship's liquid capacity is about a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship.

clue.text: Welsh woman going on about son's language

indicators.note: going on means the Welsh woman is added after the other pieces

parts.note: circa means about
S is the abbreviation for son
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman rattles on about her son.
explanation.definitionFit: Circassian is the tongue of a people of the north-west Caucasus.

clue.text: Unemployed superstar, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an idol is a superstar

explanation.surface: A star without work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means not working.

clue.text: Epic gives poor Len a real fright

indicators.note: poor suggests the words are in bad shape and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Poor Len is given a real fright by something epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something grand or heroic in scale.

clue.text: Girl's gown is in shed

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a girl; plus the 's
a robe is a gown

explanation.surface: A girl's dress is in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' reads as a noun for a hut, but it is the verb: take off clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed clothing is to undress.

clue.text: Protector has matter to drag up about university

parts.note: body means substance or matter

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the university letter
in a down clue, up means the word drag is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A protector must haul matter up around a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' makes GARD from DRAG; 'about' puts it round U to give GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodyguard is a person employed to protect someone.

clue.text: Vicious note received in the plant

indicators.note: received in means the note is taken into the plant

parts.note: a violet is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: A nasty note turned up inside the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent means brutal and savage.

clue.text: Former partner, newly attired for surrender to foreign judiciary

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: newly suggests the letters of attired are made anew

explanation.surface: An ex in new clothes hands themselves over to foreign courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Extradition is handing a suspect over to another country's justice system.

clue.text: A divine purpose originally announced in the supplements

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a divine, a clergyman
an end is a purpose

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of announced

explanation.surface: A clergyman's aims are announced in the newspaper's supplements.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are additions placed at the end of a book.

clue.text: Card-carrying actor appearing as dignified old woman

indicators.note: carrying means the actor holds the card inside

parts.note: a doer is someone who acts
a card is a joker or wag

explanation.surface: A union-card actor appears playing a stately old lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card-carrying' looks like membership, but it is a joker carried by the actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow with a title from her late husband, typically elderly and stately.

clue.text: Blow up general assembly

indicators.note: assembly suggests the letters of general are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A general assembly is blown up.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it bigger.

clue.text: Sun god enters accompanied by singular apparitions

indicators.note: enters means the sun god goes inside the other word

parts.note: with means accompanied by
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A sun god comes in with odd apparitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Wraiths are ghosts.

clue.text: Irritable when capsized cutter damaged ship

indicators.note: capsized in a down clue turns the cutter upside down

parts.note: a saw is a cutting tool

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of ship are knocked about

explanation.surface: Irritable after a capsized cutter wrecked the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' looks like a boat; it is a saw, turned over to give WAS; 'damaged' makes PISH from SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means sharply irritable.

clue.text: Acknowledges truth of page in book about church

indicators.note: about means the book goes round the church

parts.note: Acts is a book of the New Testament
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone admits a page in a book about the church is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the book wrapping both church and page; 'book' is a book of the Bible, not any volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a claim is to agree it is correct.

clue.text: Prospect reportedly observed when on eastern trains

indicators.note: reportedly signals that observed is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: seen means observed
RY, railway, means trains

explanation.surface: Views seen from eastern trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' applies only to observed: the sound of 'seen' supplies the start of the answer, before eastern and trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a view of the landscape.

clue.text: Simpleton involved in ill-considered course — a hopeless pursuit

indicators.note: involved in means the simpleton is put inside the other words

parts.note: wild means reckless or ill-considered
a chase is a course, as in a hunting run
a goose is a silly person

explanation.surface: A fool caught up in a hopeless chase.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild-goose chase is a futile search.

clue.text: A fish producing a gelatinous carbohydrate

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish yields a jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly-like substance made from seaweed.

clue.text: Hi-fi enthusiast in Douai mislaid papers, it's said

indicators.note: mislaid suggests the letters of Douai are put in the wrong order
it's said signals papers is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a file is a collection of papers

explanation.surface: A stereo buff mislaid his papers in the French town of Douai.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiophile loves high-quality sound reproduction.

clue.text: Society member prepared food around noon

indicators.note: around means the food goes round noon

parts.note: fried is a way food is prepared

explanation.surface: A club member cooks food around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Society' is the Religious Society of Friends, the Quakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Quaker movement is called a Friend.

clue.text: Having sideboards, say, the king is surrounded by drink

indicators.note: is surrounded by means the king goes inside the drink

parts.note: whisky is a drink
ER, Edwardus Rex, means King Edward

explanation.surface: The king is engulfed in drink while his sideburns grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sideboards' is British slang for sideburns, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are facial hair, so having them means being hairy-faced.
